title: Can I BEAT Rainbow Chess?
summary: 'Rainbow chess' (from a Vsauce Michael podcast clip): all 32 pieces of both colours go into a bag; pieces are drawn at random and placed on White's two ranks from a1 across (then Black's ranks), keeping their own colour, so each side's camp contains a mix of white and black pieces. Played vs Martin; Tony wins with mate in two.
rules: Put all 32 pieces (both colours) in a bag (simulated with a wheel).
Draw pieces one at a time; fill White's ranks 1-2 starting at a1 moving horizontally, then Black's ranks 7-8 the same way.
A drawn piece keeps its own colour regardless of which side's camp it lands in (e.g. a black rook on a1).
A placement that would leave a king starting in check is not allowed (e.g. black queen moved to d8 instead of d1).
Otherwise normal chess; each colour controls its own pieces wherever they start.

opponent.name: Martin
opponent.avatar_description: cartoon Martin, dark beard, brown turtleneck

setup: Randomized per game: 32 pieces shuffled across ranks 1,2,7,8 regardless of colour (first draw in video: black rook on a1), with no king in check at start.
visual_fx: Thumbnail: rainbow-coloured king among white pieces, 'Rainbow?'
current_impl_issues: Impl fairy k=rainbow swaps knights/bishops/rooks for random fairy pieces — wrong. Video uses only standard pieces randomly drawn from a mixed-colour bag and placed in both camps.

vfx_timeline.effect: wheel spin to draw each random piece, piece placed on next square
